info.title: devctl reservation and Kubernetes gateway API
info.description: Whole-cluster reservations with an administrator-controlled developer booking limit (default one), an identity-wide primary selection, and one stable /k8s gateway. CLI and kubectl plugin use OIDC exec credentials with refresh; browser downloads contain a revocable developer-scoped PAT. Login, setup, refresh and Kubernetes requests never allocate a cluster. With no active primary, gateway requests return403 text/plain with “no cluster is booked”, so native kubectl discovery and raw requests preserve the actionable message. Control API /v1/access retains409 for the same reservation conflict. Original cluster credentials stay encrypted server-side. Existing bookings survive upgrade, but legacy session-scoped PATs are revoked; old /k8s/sessions/... and /k8s/auto/... connection paths return410 and require one fresh setup/download.

get.summary: Forward a Kubernetes API request to the authenticated developer’s current primary
get.description: Stable catch-all Kubernetes API gateway, not a remote shell endpoint. Validates a trusted API JWT or developer-scoped opaque PAT, resolves the current owned active primary from server state, and pins this request to its reservation and selection version. No primary returns403 text/plain with “no cluster is booked”, preserving the message in native typed/raw kubectl clients. Other gateway rejections use Kubernetes Status JSON as documented. Requests never allocate. Streams recheck credential validity, active reservation and unchanged primary; a switch closes old streams rather than migrating them. JWT streams can continue through fresh authenticated primary heartbeats during actual activity. PAT streams recheck PAT expiry/revocation separately. Original upstream credentials remain server-side, caller identity headers are stripped, verified upstream HTTPS uses HTTP/1.1 for WebSocket/SPDY, and Kubernetes content/status/queries are preserved. Browser cookies never authenticate this route.

200.description: Upstream Kubernetes response; content type and status are preserved. Watch/log responses may stream.

101.description: Bidirectional upgraded Kubernetes stream (for example WebSocket/SPDY), passed through by the gateway.

401.description: Invalid or expired API JWT / personal token.

403.description: No active primary booking returns text/plain with an actionable booking message. Other gateway authorization denials return a Kubernetes Status JSON document.

text/plain.example: no cluster is booked; book a cluster in the web UI or with devctl start

404.description: Gateway request rejected or state unavailable.

409.description: Primary selection changed or booking ended during routing; retry the command. This is distinct from the no-primary text403 response.

502.description: Registered upstream is unavailable or its TLS/transport fails; upstream secrets are not included in the diagnostic.

503.description: Gateway request rejected or state unavailable.

default.description: Other upstream Kubernetes statuses and response content are passed through, including resource-specific errors. Do not assume all upstream responses are JSON.

400.description: Gateway request rejected or state unavailable.

405.description: Gateway request rejected or state unavailable.

No primary returns403 text/plain with “no cluster is booked”, preserving the message in native typed/raw kubectl clients. Other gateway rejections use Kubernetes Status JSON as documented. Requests never allocate. Streams recheck credential validity, active reservation and unchanged primary; a switch closes old streams rather than migrating them. JWT streams can continue through fresh authenticated primary heartbeats during actual activity. PAT streams recheck PAT expiry/revocation separately. Original upstream credentials remain server-side, caller identity headers are stripped, verified upstream HTTPS uses HTTP/1.1 for WebSocket/SPDY, and Kubernetes content/status/queries are preserved. Browser cookies never authenticate this route.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Catch-all Kubernetes suffix including slashes, for example api/v1/namespaces/default/pods. Preserved with its query string.

200.description: Upstream Kubernetes response; content type and status are preserved. Watch/log responses may stream.

101.description: Bidirectional upgraded Kubernetes stream (for example WebSocket/SPDY), passed through by the gateway.

401.description: Invalid or expired API JWT / personal token.

403.description: No active primary booking returns text/plain with an actionable booking message. Other gateway authorization denials return a Kubernetes Status JSON document.

text/plain.example: no cluster is booked; book a cluster in the web UI or with devctl start

404.description: Gateway request rejected or state unavailable.

409.description: Primary selection changed or booking ended during routing; retry the command. This is distinct from the no-primary text403 response.

502.description: Registered upstream is unavailable or its TLS/transport fails; upstream secrets are not included in the diagnostic.

503.description: Gateway request rejected or state unavailable.

default.description: Other upstream Kubernetes statuses and response content are passed through, including resource-specific errors. Do not assume all upstream responses are JSON.

400.description: Gateway request rejected or state unavailable.

405.description: Gateway request rejected or state unavailable.

requestBody.description: Kubernetes API payload, forwarded with its content type. Bodies can contain sensitive Secrets and must not be logged.

bearerAuth.description: Trusted issuer, API audience, valid signature and expiry, explicit access-token marker and approved group required. ID tokens rejected.

browserSession.name: __Host-devctl-web
browserSession.description: Opaque Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie; OAuth credentials remain encrypted server-side. Cookie-authenticated POST/PATCH/DELETE require the exact configured Origin and X-CSRF-Token from /web/session. Cookies never authenticate Kubernetes gateway requests.

personalToken.description: Opaque dcpat_ personal credential accepted ONLY by /k8s. It follows that authenticated developer’s current active primary and cannot call control/admin APIs, book, switch primary or refresh itself. Default8h/max168h, independent of booking TTL; individually revocable. No booking is needed to issue it.

last_activity_at.description: Last accepted Kubernetes API request or authorized open stream observation; control-plane heartbeat calls do not count as activity.

primary.description: Whether this active booking is its owner’s current primary. First booking is selected automatically; later bookings do not switch it.

ttl.description: Optional Go duration, 1m through 168h; omitted means no expiry

kubeconfig.description: Administrator-only import of one portable context with static embedded token or certificate/key and verified HTTPS. Encrypted immediately, used only by the backend transport, and never returned to developers.

server.description: Stable configured public HTTPS origin plus /k8s. It contains no session, binding or developer identifier. The authenticated identity determines the primary cluster on the backend; setup does not reserve a cluster.

certificate_authority_data.description: Optional base64-encoded public PEM CA data for gateway TLS, never upstream client credentials.

scope.description: New credentials use kubernetes:primary. Historical legacy credentials may be listed with a different scope and are revoked during migration.

PersonalAccessToken.description: Public credential metadata only; digest and secret are never listed. Expiry is independent of booking TTL, so a valid PAT can access a later explicitly booked primary for the same identity.

ttl.description: 1m through168h, default8h. Independent of booking expiry; no sliding renewal.

kubeconfig.description: Sensitive one-time gateway-only YAML using the stable /k8s URL and an opaque developer PAT. No exec helper, OIDC refresh/access/ID token, original Kubernetes endpoint or upstream credential. Create without a booking; keep the same file across explicit booking changes until PAT expiry/revocation.

owner_id.description: Stable ownership key derived from trusted issuer plus subject; never email.

max_bookings.description: Effective identity-wide maximum active bookings, including shared bookings.

max_bookings_override.description: Optional administrator override. Absence means inherit the current global default.

primary_session.description: Current owned active primary, omitted when no booking exists.

selection_version.description: Changes when the primary changes; gateway streams remain pinned to the version they started with.

cluster.description: An owned active cluster ID, display name, or booking ID.

authorization_expires_at.description: Current server authorization lease for this exact primary version. May be the zero UTC timestamp before gateway authorization. A fresh JWT heartbeat may renew it only during actual recent Kubernetes activity; capped by JWT expiry and booking expiry.
